question: does the per-arm fetch budget (24 rounds) survive a 48-turn tools-on cell, and what happens to the turns after it closes
answer_detail: In the modern tools-on shape (per-turn cap 3 + serve-from-prompt) the budget never closed: 20 of 24 rounds were billed, the last one at T16, and T17-T48 billed 0. Zero fetch_budget_exhausted refusals appear in the cell's 371 tool calls, so no turn ran with the channel shut and all 48 turns are measurement. The one closure on disk is the pre-V6 configuration (no per-turn cap), which closed at T3 and produced 45 confounded turns; that closure is why the per-turn cap was added.
era_note: never pooled: v4/v5 rows ran the V5 runner (no per-turn cap, TOOL_SERVE_FROM_PROMPT absent); v6 rows ran the V6 runner (per-turn cap 3, serve-from-prompt on)

exhaustion_behaviour.quote: elif rounds_used + fresh >= TOOL_FETCH_ROUNDS_PER_ARM: ... rec = {..., "billed": False, "error": "fetch_budget_exhausted"} ... blocks.append('<tool_result error="fetch_budget_exhausted"/>')
semantics: per CALL, not per turn: a range already pinned in the prompt is still served (served_from=prompt) and still costs no round, so a checkpoint read stays servable after the rounds are gone (run_longrun.py:941-946)
the refusal spends nothing and bills nothing (billed=False); the model receives an empty <tool_result> and is asked to answer
no exit code is raised at the round boundary; the row records the refusal inside tool_calls[].error, and no field marks the channel closed
the per-turn bound refuses separately as per_turn_round_cap (run_longrun.py:912-918), and the per-turn call ceiling as turn_call_cap (run_longrun.py:955-958)
exhaustion_behaviour.why_no_marker: the refusal is per call, so the channel is not a binary state on the row: the next turn may still be served from a pinned body. What the row shows is the error string, not a closed channel.

per_file.caveat: this era billed rounds that errored path_not_found (fresh += 1 on every executed attempt); its 20 rounds are not a demand measurement for the modern shape

per_file.closes_by_single_turn: T3 alone bought 21 of the 24 rounds

post_closure.completion_tokens_nonzero_distribution_n: one count of a 4,096-token completion in 45 post-closure turns; reported as a count, not a rate
post_closure.answer_length_note: T36 emitted 25 refused calls for 779 completion tokens and T29 emitted 130 for 4,096; both are the inspection the model could not perform

invitation_after_closure.census_rule: invites-read = the question names a source path (*.py, *.py#L..., *.md, *.json, *.txt) - GRID-SHAPE.md:32 and the GRID-SHAPE-TOOLS census

independent_reproduction.result: 46 of 48 turn blocks carry a path reference in both; the two that do not are T30 and T48

v5_post_closure.model_behaviour: 41 of 45 post-closure turns emitted tool_calls anyway; 226 were refused host-side with fetch_budget_exhausted and received an empty <tool_result>
v5_post_closure.verdict: the invitation persists while the channel is shut - the degeneration condition is present, and the model acts on it

invitation_after_closure.v6_note: no post-closure turn exists in v6: the budget never closed

arithmetic_for_the_fix.identity: price = turns + rounds + digests; per cell price = turns/10 + B, grid = 480 + 10*B + 4

recommendation.rationale: 2.4x the largest measured 48-turn cell demand (20), one round per turn by construction, and cheap: +240 requests over the frozen 724
recommendation.structural_note: 48 is not proof: with the per-turn cap at 3, a cell spending the cap for 16 consecutive turns still closes at T16. Only 144 (3 x 48) makes closure impossible in a 48-turn cell.

per_cell_budget_flag.observed: GRID-SHAPE.json cell flags carry --budget 67 while the same cells project 48 + 24 = 72 requests
per_cell_budget_flag.consequence: any allowance above 19 makes turns + rounds exceed 67; raising the fetch budget without raising --budget converts a fetch-budget question into a BudgetExhausted exit (run_longrun.py:961 raises BudgetExhausted)
per_cell_budget_flag.action: the separate budget-change card must raise --budget to at least turns + B

arithmetic_for_the_fix.headroom_discrepancy_in_the_card: the card cites 'remaining 3,192' once; the ledger figure is 3,219 (REQUEST-LEDGER.json budget.cap 4320, spent 1101, remaining 3219). 3,192 is treated as a transposition and not used

headroom.note: the card's 3,192 is the fresh-scan figure, not a transposition; the frozen artefact is stale by 27 requests. Two pre-existing tests fail on that drift (test_request_ledger_dedup.py::TestRealCorpus::test_6, test_request_ledger_sound.py::TestPublishedArtefact::test_11) - neither is caused by this unit.

earliest_structural_closure.arithmetic: 24 rounds / 3 per turn = 8 turns at the per-turn cap

residual_risk.why: the canary runs 5 turns (docs/TRANCHE-CANARY.md:24, default N=5); exhaustion cannot occur before T8, so a 5-turn window cannot observe this failure mode at all. The canary protects the cap-length degeneration (first observed at T3) and does not protect fetch-budget exhaustion.

stop_rule_that_bounds_the_residual.on_disk: RUN-A-STAR-2 is absent (grep for STAR-2: zero hits); orchestration/units/RUN-A-STAR.md:18 carries stop rules 1-7 only
stop_rule_that_bounds_the_residual.mechanism_that_actually_fires: experiments/ptr-engine/longrun/run_longrun.py:2560 - 'if signature and ceiling_violations + 1 >= runaway_turns:' with runaway_turns frozen at 2 (--runaway-turns 2); the second cap-length completion ends the run with exit 6
stop_rule_that_bounds_the_residual.does_it_fire_before_the_cell_is_useless: it fires after 2 cap-length completions, so the cell has already spent >=2 turns (>=8192 completion tokens) answering nothing. It bounds the residual by aborting loudly rather than letting confounded turns accumulate; it does not preserve the cell.

headroom_discrepancy_in_the_card: resolved: 3,192 is the fresh-scan remaining (spent 1128); the frozen ledger artefact still says 3,219 (spent 1101). Use 3,192 conservatively. Ledger artefacts were NOT edited.
